# Learning Objectives

By the end of this lecture, you will be able to:

- Explain what R Markdown is and why it is used for reproducible research
- Understand the **three layers** of an R Markdown document: YAML, Markdown text, and R code chunks
- Configure a YAML header for HTML, PDF, and Word outputs
- Control chunk behaviour with key options: `echo`, `eval`, `include`, `message`, `warning`
- Use inline R code to embed live results in narrative text
- Structure documents with headings, lists, bold/italic text, tables, links, and images
- Apply **tabsets** for interactive section navigation
- Use the **visual editor** and publish to **RPubs**
- Understand and apply advanced YAML options: `toc_float`, `code_folding`, `theme`, `highlight`, `number_sections`

---

# What is R Markdown?

R Markdown is a file format (`.Rmd`) that **combines R code, its output, and narrative text** in a single document. When you *knit* the document, R Markdown runs all the code, collects the results, and weaves everything into a polished output file.

## Why R Markdown?

| Benefit | Description |
|---|---|
| **Reproducibility** | Anyone with the `.Rmd` file can regenerate the exact same results |
| **Multiple output formats** | One source file → HTML, PDF, Word, slides |
| **Automation** | Reports update automatically when data changes |
| **Transparency** | Code and results live together — no copy-paste errors |
| **Portfolio building** | Publish to RPubs or GitHub to showcase your work |

## Output formats at a glance

| Format | Requirement | Use case |
|---|---|---|
| `html_document` | None — always available | Web reports, interactive documents |
| `pdf_document` | LaTeX installed (MiKTeX / TinyTeX) | Academic papers, formal reports |
| `word_document` | Microsoft Word or LibreOffice | Collaborating with non-R users |
| `beamer_presentation` | LaTeX | PDF slide deck |
| `ioslides_presentation` | None | HTML slide deck |

> **Getting started with PDF:** Install TinyTeX directly from R:  
> `install.packages("tinytex"); tinytex::install_tinytex()`

---

# The Three Layers of an R Markdown Document

Every `.Rmd` file has exactly three layers:

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  1. YAML HEADER (metadata & output options) │  ← between --- delimiters
├─────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  2. MARKDOWN TEXT (narrative, prose)        │  ← plain text + formatting
├─────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  3. R CODE CHUNKS (executable R code)       │  ← between ```{r} and ```
└─────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

---

# Layer 1 — The YAML Header

The YAML header sits at the very top of the `.Rmd` file, surrounded by triple dashes (`---`). It controls the document's **metadata** (title, author, date) and **rendering options** (output format, themes, table of contents).

## Minimal YAML

```yaml
---
title: "My Report"
author: "Your Name"
date: "`r Sys.Date()`"
output: html_document
---
```

> `"\`r Sys.Date()\`"` is inline R code inside YAML — the date updates automatically every time you knit.

## Full-featured HTML YAML

```yaml
---
title: "My Report"
author: "Your Name"
date: "`r Sys.Date()`"
output:
  html_document:
    toc: true               # Include a table of contents
    toc_float: true         # Make the TOC float on the left as you scroll
    toc_depth: 3            # Include headings up to level 3
    number_sections: true   # Auto-number all sections
    fig_caption: true       # Show captions below figures
    theme: flatly           # Bootstrap CSS theme
    highlight: tango        # Syntax highlighting style for code
    code_folding: hide      # Hide code blocks by default (reader can expand)
editor_options:
  markdown:
    wrap: 72                # Wrap text at 72 characters per line
---
```

## Generating multiple output formats from one file

```yaml
---
title: "My Report"
author: "Your Name"
output:
  html_document:
    toc: true
    toc_float: true
  pdf_document:
    toc: true
  word_document:
    toc: true
---
```

> **Note:** When multiple output formats are listed, clicking *Knit* produces the **first** format listed. Use `rmarkdown::render("file.Rmd", output_format = "all")` to render all formats at once.

## Complete YAML option reference

### `theme` — Bootstrap CSS themes for HTML

Available themes:

| Theme | Style |
|---|---|
| `default` | Standard, clean |
| `cerulean` | Blue accent, modern |
| `flatly` | Flat design, professional |
| `cosmo` | Clean and minimal |
| `journal` | Classic academic |
| `readable` | Optimised for reading |
| `spacelab` | Light grey, spacious |
| `united` | Orange accent |
| `darkly` | Dark background |
| `lumen` | Soft pastel tones |

### `highlight` — Syntax highlighting for code chunks

| Style | Character |
|---|---|
| `default` | Standard |
| `tango` | Warm earth tones |
| `pygments` | Colourful, Python-inspired |
| `kate` | Cool blue/green |
| `monochrome` | Black and white |
| `espresso` | Dark, elegant |
| `zenburn` | Low-contrast, eye-friendly |
| `haddock` | Modern, high contrast |
| `textmate` | Bright, editor-like |

### `code_folding`

```yaml
code_folding: hide    # Code hidden by default; reader clicks to expand
code_folding: show    # Code visible by default; reader can collapse
code_folding: none    # No toggle button — always use chunk-level echo
```

# Layer 2 — Markdown Text

## Headings

```markdown
# Heading Level 1
## Heading Level 2
### Heading Level 3
#### Heading Level 4
##### Heading Level 5
###### Heading Level 6
```

## Text Formatting

```markdown
**Bold text**
*Italic text*
***Bold and italic***
~~Strikethrough~~
`inline code`
```

**Bold text** | *Italic text* | ***Bold and italic*** | ~~Strikethrough~~ | `inline code`

## Lists

Unordered list (use `-`, `*`, or `+`):

```markdown
- First item
- Second item
  - Nested item
  - Another nested item
- Third item
```

Ordered list:

```markdown
1. First step
2. Second step
3. Third step
```

## Links and Images

```markdown
[Link text](https://www.example.com)

![Image caption](path/to/image.png)
```

## Tables

```markdown
| Column 1 | Column 2 | Column 3 |
|----------|----------|----------|
| Cell 1   | Cell 2   | Cell 3   |
| Cell 4   | Cell 5   | Cell 6   |
```

| Column 1 | Column 2 | Column 3 |
|----------|----------|----------|
| Cell 1   | Cell 2   | Cell 3   |
| Cell 4   | Cell 5   | Cell 6   |

## Block quotes

```markdown
> This is a block quote.
> It can span multiple lines.
```

> This is a block quote.  
> It can span multiple lines.

## Horizontal rule

```markdown
---
```

---

## Tabsets `{.tabset}`

Tabsets are an HTML feature that turns sub-headings into clickable tabs — very useful for organising related plots or tables without cluttering the page.

To create a tabset, add `{.tabset}` to the **parent heading**:

````markdown
## Results {.tabset}

### Plot
```{r}
plot(iris$Sepal.Length)
```

### Table
```{r}
head(iris)
```
````

## Results {.tabset}

### Plot

```{r tabset-plot}
plot(iris$Sepal.Length, col = "steelblue", pch = 16,
     main = "Iris Sepal Length", ylab = "cm")
```

### Table

```{r tabset-table}
head(iris, 10)
```

### Summary

```{r tabset-summary}
summary(iris)
```

# Layer 3 — R Code Chunks

A code chunk is delimited by three backticks and `{r}`:

````markdown
```{r chunk-name, option1 = value1, option2 = value2}
# Your R code here
```
````

## Key chunk options

| Option | Values | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `echo` | `TRUE` / `FALSE` | Show or hide the code in the output |
| `eval` | `TRUE` / `FALSE` | Run or skip the code |
| `include` | `TRUE` / `FALSE` | Run code but show/hide both code AND output |
| `message` | `TRUE` / `FALSE` | Show or hide package loading messages |
| `warning` | `TRUE` / `FALSE` | Show or hide warning messages |
| `fig.width` | numeric | Figure width in inches |
| `fig.height` | numeric | Figure height in inches |
| `fig.cap` | `"string"` | Caption below a figure |
| `cache` | `TRUE` / `FALSE` | Cache results (avoids rerunning slow chunks) |

## Demonstration of chunk options

### `echo = TRUE` — Code and output both shown

```{r echo-true, echo=TRUE}
summary(rnorm(1000, mean = 0, sd = 1))
```

### `echo = FALSE` — Output shown, code hidden

```{r echo-false, echo=FALSE}
cat("This result appears, but you cannot see the code that produced it.\n")
```

### `eval = FALSE` — Code shown, NOT executed

```{r eval-false, eval=FALSE}
# This code will appear in the document but will NOT run
summary(cars)
```

### `include = FALSE` — Code runs silently, nothing shown

```{r include-false, include=FALSE}
x <- 42   # This runs, x is now in memory, but nothing appears in the document
```

> The variable `x` created above equals `r x` — we can use it in inline code!

### `message = FALSE` and `warning = FALSE`

```{r message-warning, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)   # Loading messages are suppressed
```

## Setting global chunk defaults

In the `setup` chunk at the top of your document, use `knitr::opts_chunk$set()` to apply default options to **all chunks**:

```{r global-opts, eval=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo    = TRUE,
  message = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE,
  fig.width  = 7,
  fig.height = 5,
  fig.align  = "center"
)
```

> Individual chunk options **override** global defaults when they conflict.

# Inline R Code

Inline R code embeds a live R expression directly into your narrative text. The syntax is: `` `r expression` ``

**Example:**

```markdown
The `iris` dataset has `r nrow(iris)` rows and `r ncol(iris)` columns.
The mean sepal length is `r round(mean(iris$Sepal.Length), 2)` cm.
```

**Renders as:**

The `iris` dataset has `r nrow(iris)` rows and `r ncol(iris)` columns.  
The mean sepal length is `r round(mean(iris$Sepal.Length), 2)` cm.

> **Why this is powerful:** If your dataset changes, the numbers in the text update automatically when you re-knit — no manual copy-pasting required.

---

# The Visual Editor

RStudio's **Visual Editor** provides a rich-text interface for writing R Markdown documents — similar to Word. To switch between Source and Visual mode, click the button in the top-left corner of the editor pane.

**What the Visual Editor makes easier:**

- Inserting links, images, and footnotes via point-and-click menus
- Formatting text with toolbar buttons (bold, italic, headings)
- Inserting tables with a graphical table editor
- Real-time markdown rendering in the editor

> **Recommended practice:** Use the Visual Editor for writing prose and inserting non-code elements. Switch to Source view when you need to fine-tune YAML, chunk options, or complex layouts.

# Publishing to RPubs

**RPubs** (https://rpubs.com) is a free hosting service by RStudio for sharing HTML R Markdown documents publicly. It functions as an online portfolio for your R work.

## How to publish

1. Knit your document to HTML
2. Click the **Publish** button (blue icon) in the Viewer pane
3. Select **RPubs**
4. Create a free account or log in
5. Give your document a title and slug (URL)
6. Click **Publish**

Your document is now live at: `https://rpubs.com/yourusername/document-slug`

## Why use RPubs?

- **Portfolio:** Add your RPubs URL to your CV to demonstrate R skills
- **Sharing:** Send a single link instead of a file attachment
- **Reference:** Others can view and learn from your code
- **Documentation:** Permanent record of your analyses

> **Important:** RPubs only supports **HTML** output. You cannot publish PDF documents to RPubs.

# Complete Reproducible Example

Here is a complete, minimal R Markdown workflow demonstrating all the concepts covered in this lecture:

```{r full-example, fig.cap="Sepal Length distribution by Species — iris dataset"}
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(iris, aes(x = Species, y = Sepal.Length, fill = Species)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7) +
  labs(
    title    = "Sepal Length by Iris Species",
    subtitle = paste("Based on", nrow(iris), "observations"),
    x        = "Species",
    y        = "Sepal Length (cm)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

The figure above shows the distribution of sepal length across the `r nlevels(iris$Species)` iris species. The overall mean sepal length is **`r round(mean(iris$Sepal.Length), 2)` cm**, with *`r iris$Species[which.max(iris$Sepal.Length)]`* having the single longest sepal at `r max(iris$Sepal.Length)` cm.

# Summary

| Concept | Key point |
|---|---|
| YAML header | Controls metadata and output format options |
| `toc` / `toc_float` | Table of contents (scrolling in HTML) |
| `theme` / `highlight` | Visual style for HTML output |
| `code_folding` | Let readers show/hide code |
| `echo` / `eval` / `include` | Control visibility and execution of chunks |
| `message` / `warning` | Suppress noisy output |
| Inline code | `` `r expr` `` — live values in narrative text |
| Tabsets | `## Section {.tabset}` — clickable tabs in HTML |
| Visual Editor | Rich-text editing mode in RStudio |
| RPubs | Free online hosting for HTML documents |

# Practice Exercises

1. Create a new `.Rmd` file. Add a YAML header that outputs to HTML with a floating TOC, the `cerulean` theme, `tango` highlighting, and `code_folding: hide`. Knit it.

2. Add three sections with headings. In each section, include one code chunk and one paragraph with at least one piece of inline R code.

3. Create a tabset with three tabs: one showing a plot of `mtcars`, one showing `head(mtcars)`, and one showing `summary(mtcars)`.

4. Write a chunk that loads `ggplot2` with `message = FALSE`. Then write a second chunk with `echo = FALSE` that plots a histogram of `mpg` from `mtcars`. Only the plot should appear.

5. *Challenge:* Publish a complete 1-page analysis of the `airquality` dataset to RPubs. Include a table of contents, at least two plots, and a conclusion paragraph with three inline R values.
